bio.statement: The county clerk page says McMullen has served as the elected Clackamas County Clerk since 2023.
bio.excerpt: She has served as the elected County Clerk since 2023.

bio.statement: The county clerk page says McMullen worked as a public librarian and, since 2015, as an elections administrator.
bio.excerpt: Clerk Catherine McMullen has devoted her career to public service, first as a public librarian, and since 2015 as an elections administrator.

verification.note: The excerpt stopped before the 2015/elections-administrator part of the statement, so it was extended to the full sentence (verified verbatim).

bio.statement: The county clerk page lists an Executive Masters in Public Administration from Portland State University's Hatfield School of Government.
bio.excerpt: She has an Executive Masters in Public Administration (EMPA) from the Portland State University Hatfield School of Government

verification.note: The statement names the Hatfield School, which the excerpt cut off. Extended the excerpt (verified verbatim).

bio.statement: McMullen's pamphlet statement lists her as a Certified County Clerk through the Oregon Association of County Clerks.
bio.excerpt: Certified County Clerk – Oregon Association of County Clerks; Masters Public Administration and Library Information Science

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, McMullen lists protecting democracy by ensuring free, fair and unbiased elections as a priority.
positions.excerpt: Protect Democracy: Ensure free, fair, unbiased elections.

positions.statement: McMullen's pamphlet statement says she will continue clear communication, timely results and public observation of elections.
positions.excerpt: Focus on Transparency: Continue clear communication, timely results, public observation.

positions.statement: McMullen's pamphlet statement says she wants to increase voter education and citizen participation and build community partnerships.
positions.excerpt: Expand Access: Increase voter education and citizen participation, build community partnerships.

positions.statement: McMullen's pamphlet statement says she will keep marriage licenses and property recording cost-effective with convenient weekday access.
positions.excerpt: Keep Services Affordable: Maintain cost-effective marriage licenses, property recording, convenient weekday access.

positions.statement: McMullen's campaign site says she led the removal of racist language from property deeds.
positions.excerpt: Led the removal of racist language from property deeds

verification.note: T2 confirmed: the county pamphlet statement prints 'ClackamasVoice.org'. The site's paid-for-by line is 'Voices for Catherine McMullen (21544)'. The excerpt is a verbatim bullet under 'Beyond elections, Catherine has:'.

positions.statement: In a September 2026 KPTV report on mail voting, McMullen says her office takes safety and security precautions for each election.
positions.excerpt: "Every election presents its own challenges and we take safety and security precautions for each one," said Catherine McMullen, Clackamas County Clerk.

verification_summary.balance_notes: Clerk race: McMullen has 10 items (T1 pamphlet and county clerk page, one T2, one T3 KPTV) and Reaksecker has 8 (all T1 pamphlet). The gap comes from the incumbent's official county bio page and a 2026 KPTV quote. Reaksecker's site markforcountyclerk.com (printed in the pamphlet) blocks fetching, and no T3 coverage exists; both are documented in his gaps. The verifier's spot-search found no missed T1/T2/T3 material for either candidate. Effort looks equal.
